newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM dampens rumours of early polls - official.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM dampens rumours of early polls - official.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Friday dampened growing media speculation that he plans to dissolve parliament and call a snap general election in October or early November.

Hashimoto denied front-page reports in Japan's major dailies on Friday that he had acceded to calls from his Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) for early elections for the Lower House of parliament, Economic Planning Agency Minister Shusei Tanaka told a news conference.

The government must first try to solve a festering dispute over U.S. military bases on the southern island of Okinawa before it holds general elections, Tanaka quoted Hashimoto as saying at a morning cabinet meeting. Okinawa holds a referendum on Sunday on the future of the bases.
Three major dailies, the liberal Asahi Shimbun, the conservative Yomiuri Shimbun and the business newspaper Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Hashimoto would call polls between October 20 and November 10.
Hashimoto does not have to call elections until mid-1997, when the four-year term of the current Lower House expires.

The newspapers cited unnamed senior officials in the ruling coalition as saying Hashimoto, believed to have been planning to wait until after January to dissolve parliament, had changed his mind under growing pressure from within the LDP, the biggest party in the coalition.

The coalition leaders cited concern about a campaign by the main opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) against an unpopular plan to raise the consumption tax to five percent from the current three percent next April, the papers said.
Hashimoto took office in January at the head of a three-party coalition of the LDP, the Social Democratic Party and New Party Sakigake.

The vote by Okinawans on Sunday is Japan's first ever referendum on U.S. military bases -- a nonbinding poll predicted to give overwhelming support for Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota's campaign to trim bases in the prefecture.
